title: CloudFront Caching & Edge Compute
summary: Cache content close to users and run code at the edge with CloudFront Functions or Lambda@Edge.
tldr: **CloudFront** caches static and dynamic content at edge locations and carries cache misses over the AWS backbone. One distribution can front S3 for `/static/*` and an ALB for the API.

Low cache hit ratio? Shrink the **cache key** with a **cache policy** (only the query strings, headers and cookies that change the response), and send everything else the origin needs with an **origin request policy**.

Lightweight header or URL logic → **CloudFront Functions** (sub-millisecond, cheapest). Network calls, body access or origin selection from data → **Lambda@Edge**. Many edges hammering one origin → **Origin Shield**.

keyFacts.text: Every header, cookie or query string in the cache key splits the cache. Values the origin needs but that don't change the response belong in the **origin request policy**.
**CloudFront Functions** run JavaScript on viewer request and viewer response only, with no network or body access, at millions of requests per second.
**Lambda@Edge** functions are authored in N. Virginia and replicated. They run on viewer or origin events, can call other services, but have no VPC access or arm64.
**Origin Shield** adds one regional cache in front of the origin, so duplicate misses from many edge locations collapse into one origin fetch.
**Origin failover** retries a secondary origin when the primary returns chosen 5xx/4xx codes or times out. It applies to GET, HEAD and OPTIONS requests.

keywords.cue: add security headers and rewrite URLs, lowest cost, sub-millisecond
pick the origin per user from a DynamoDB lookup
cache hit ratio below 5%, all headers and cookies forwarded
keywords.answer: Narrow cache policy + origin request policy for what the origin needs

keywords.cue: origin overloaded by duplicate requests from many edge locations
keep serving if the S3 bucket's Region fails, no DNS change
keywords.answer: S3 CRR + CloudFront origin group failover

keywords.cue: global users, slow static assets, private bucket
keywords.answer: CloudFront with S3 origin and origin access control (OAC)

keywords.cue: cheaper Lambda@Edge for simple viewer logic

traps: Increasing TTLs doesn't help when the cache key includes every cookie and header; nearly every request is still unique.
CloudFront Functions can't make network calls, so they can't read DynamoDB.
Origin Shield reduces origin load; it isn't failover. Failover needs an **origin group**.
S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads to one bucket; it doesn't cache content for global readers.
Global Accelerator doesn't cache. For repeated content downloads, CloudFront is the right edge service.
